# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Governing Policy:** Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I) — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf

**Member:** Jordan Iverson
**Member ID:** W979574719
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-20
**Reference Number:** POC-E6EF62D505-92473
**Payer:** UnitedHealthcare / Oxford
**Plan/Product:** Commercial/ACA, State of Connecticut

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), which was denied on 2026-08-20 as not medically necessary (reference number POC-E6EF62D505-92473). I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision and to approve the procedure my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has determined is needed.

## Why I believe this decision should be reversed

The denial was issued under the plan's own policy, *Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)*. That policy states:

> "Coverage Rationale Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

My medical records show that my circumstances are exactly the kind the policy contemplates as medically necessary. Specifically:

- **Diagnosis and imaging.** My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-06-17, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. On exam, I have a neurologic deficit corresponding to this imaged level, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and radicular pain radiating into my right calf. Functionally, I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes at a time.

- **Failed conservative care.** The policy recognizes that surgery is appropriate when conservative treatment does not resolve the pain:

  > "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)."

  My records document that I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26) focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have progressed over 9 months despite this treatment.

- **Recognized surgical indication for stenosis.** The policy also acknowledges that lumbar stenosis is commonly treated surgically when conservative measures fail:

  > "Lumbar Fusion for Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Alone Lumbar spinal stenosis is a common degenerative condition and a frequent indication for surgical intervention when conservative treatment fails."

  While this language appears under a fusion-specific heading and my procedure is a decompression, it reflects the plan's own recognition that stenosis unresponsive to conservative treatment is a recognized reason for surgical intervention. My MRI documents severe stenosis at the level matching my symptoms, and my conservative treatment did not resolve my pain or function.

I also have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke — none of which the policy identifies as a barrier to coverage.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The denial notice states that my request was reviewed against "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," and the policy itself directs reviewers to InterQual® criteria for the specific clinical coverage requirements ("Procedures, Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar (Custom) - UHG Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."). InterQual is licensed software, not a document I have access to. Under ERISA and ACA appeal rules, I am entitled to receive, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on in denying my claim. I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, so that I and my surgeon can respond to the specific standard used.

## What I am asking for

I ask that the plan reconsider this denial in light of my diagnostic imaging, documented neurologic findings, and my extended, unsuccessful course of conservative treatment, and that it provide the specific InterQual criteria applied to my case as requested above.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-16. I will submit this appeal through member.uhc.com and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, and I will also send it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed.

Thank you for reviewing my appeal.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Jordan Iverson
Member ID: W979574719
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

---

**Enclosures:** Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-17–2026-06-26); MRI lumbar spine report (2026-06-17); corticosteroid injection record (2026-04-02); office/exam notes from Dr. Lindqvist

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
